dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:1701.text: To deny or brazenly dispute a charge, or to evade responsibility. Formed from 言, with 闌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1702.text: To examine. Formed from 言, with 㐱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1703.text: A sorrowful sound. Formed from 言, with abbreviated 斯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1704.text: A fault or crime. Formed from 言, with 尤 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Repay him with the many offenses.”

shuowen:1705.text: To bring to account. Formed from 言, with 朱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1706.text: To put in order or deal with. Formed from 言 and 寸.

shuowen:1707.text: To know thoroughly. Formed from 言, with 音 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1708.text: To pray, recounting merits and virtues in seeking blessings. The Analects says: “The invocation says: ‘We pray for you to the spirits above and below.’” Formed from 言, with abbreviated 纍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1709.text: A trace of one's conduct, a posthumous title. Formed from 言, 兮 and 皿. The explanation is incomplete.

shuowen:1710.text: A posthumous eulogy or title. Formed from 言, with 耒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1711.text: Shame. Formed from 言, with 奚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1712.text: 謑詬: shame. Formed from 言, with 后 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1713.text: A counterspy in an army. Formed from 言, with 枼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1714.text: An agreement or signal within an army. Formed from 言, with 亥 indicating the sound. Read like 該 in “the heart full.” [The pronunciation phrase is obscure.]

shuowen:1715.text: One who transmits and interprets the speech of the peoples of the four quarters. Formed from 言, with 睪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1716.text: To press upon. Formed from 言, with 九 indicating the sound. Read like 求.

shuowen:1717.text: The appearance of laughter. Formed from 言, with 益 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1718.text: Rapid speech. Formed from three 言. Read like 沓.

shuowen:1719.text: To consult or deliberate. Formed from 言, with 旬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1720.text: Upright speech. Formed from 言, with 黨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1721.text: A register or record. Formed from 言, with 普 indicating the sound. The Records of the Historian forms it from 並.

shuowen:1722.text: 詎 is like 豈, “how could” or “surely not.” Formed from 言, with 巨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1723.text: Small; to entice. Formed from 言, with 叜 indicating the sound. The Record of Rites says: “Enough to entice one's hearing.”

shuowen:1724.text: A concealed saying or riddle. Formed from 言 and 迷; 迷 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1725.text: A record. Formed from 言, with 志 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1726.text: To take final leave. Another explanation: a method. Formed from 言, with abbreviated 決 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1727.text: Competing in speech. Formed from two 言. All characters in the 誩 category are formed from 誩. Read like 競.

shuowen:1728.text: Good or auspicious. Formed from 誩 and 羊, sharing the underlying idea of 義 and 美.

shuowen:1729.text: Forceful speech. Another explanation: to pursue or compete. Formed from 誩 and two 人.

shuowen:1730.text: Bitter resentment. Formed from 誩, with 𧷏 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “The people have no resentful complaints.”

shuowen:1731.text: Sound arising in the heart and articulated outwardly is called 音. Gong, shang, jue, zhi and yu are 聲; silk, bamboo, metal, stone, gourd, clay, leather and wood are 音. Formed from 言 containing 一. All characters in the 音 category are formed from 音.

shuowen:1732.text: Sound or resonance. Formed from 音, with 鄉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1733.text: A low, penetrating sound. Formed from 音, with 酓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1734.text: The music of Shun of Yu. The Documents says: “When the Nine Sections of the Xiao Shao were completed, phoenixes came in stately attendance.” Formed from 音, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1735.text: A completed passage of music is one 章. Formed from 音 and 十; 十 is the end of the numbers.

shuowen:1736.text: The completion of a musical piece is 竟. Formed from 音 and 人.

shuowen:1737.text: Harmony. Formed from 音, with 員 indicating the sound. Pei Guangyuan says it was anciently the same as 均; whether this is correct is unknown.

shuowen:1738.text: Crime or fault. Formed from 干 and 二; 二 is the ancient form of 上. All characters in the 䇂 category are formed from 䇂. Read like 愆. Zhang Lin's explanation.

shuowen:1739.text: A male convicted of a crime is called a 奴, and a 奴 is called 童; a female is called 妾. Formed from 䇂, with abbreviated 重 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1740.text: A woman convicted of a crime who serves and may attend the lord. Formed from 䇂 and 女. The Spring and Autumn says: “The woman became someone's concubine.” A 妾 is not formally betrothed.

shuowen:1741.text: Plants growing in clumps. It depicts clumped peaks emerging side by side. All characters in the 丵 category are formed from 丵. Read like 浞.

shuowen:1742.text: A large board decorating suspended bells and drums. Its edges are cut like saw teeth and painted white; it depicts interlocking projections supporting one another. Formed from 丵 and 巾; 巾 depicts the board. The Odes says: “The large 業 boards and the upright supports.”

shuowen:1743.text: To gather. Formed from 丵, with 取 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1744.text: To answer or respond in a way suited to the question, rather than by a fixed formula. Formed from 丵, 口 and 寸.

shuowen:1745.text: To press importunately or repeatedly trouble someone, as in the expression 瀆菐. Formed from 丵 and 廾; 廾 also indicates the sound. All characters in the 菐 category are formed from 菐.

shuowen:1746.text: One who serves. Formed from 人 and 菐; 菐 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1747.text: To assign tasks. Formed from 菐 and 八; 八 means to divide and also indicates the sound. Read like 頒; another pronunciation is like 非.

shuowen:1748.text: To raise the hands. Formed from 𠂇 and 又. All characters in the 廾 category are formed from 廾. (Clerical writing now changes it to 廾.)

shuowen:1749.text: To support or receive respectfully. Formed from 手 and 廾, with 𡴀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1750.text: To assist. Formed from 廾, 卩 and 山. The height of 山 conveys supporting and upholding.

shuowen:1751.text: Large, spacious or splendid; an alternative sense related to taking or seizing is reported but remains obscure. Formed from 廾 and an abbreviated 夐. [Duan states that the first gloss 取奐 is not understood.]

shuowen:1752.text: To cover. Formed from 廾 and 合.

shuowen:1753.text: To draw forth and supply. Formed from 廾, with 睪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1754.text: To lift. Formed from 廾, with 甶 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Some Jin men fell with their broad chariot; the Chu men lifted it.” Huang Hao explains: the broad chariot became stuck, and Chu men lifted it for them. Du Lin takes it as a character for 騏麟.

shuowen:1755.text: To raise. Formed from 廾, with 㠯 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “The Four Mountains said: ‘Raise him up!’”

shuowen:1756.text: To play with. Formed from 廾 holding 玉.

shuowen:1757.text: To hold something fully in both hands. Formed from 廾, with 𡴆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1758.text: To form rice into a ball with the hands. Formed from 廾, with 釆 indicating the sound. 釆 is the ancient form of 辦. Read like 卷 in 書卷, a book scroll.

shuowen:1759.text: To hold the stock of a crossbow. Formed from 廾 and 肉. Read like 逵.

shuowen:1760.text: To be on guard. Formed from 廾 holding 戈, guarding against the unexpected.

shuowen:1761.text: Weapons or implements. Formed from 廾 holding 斤, depicting combined strength.

shuowen:1762.text: Honest and cautious. Formed from 廾, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1763.text: The board game weiqi. Formed from 廾, with 亦 indicating the sound. The Analects says: “Are there not the games bo and yi?”

shuowen:1764.text: To provide and set out together. Formed from 廾 and abbreviated 貝; anciently shells were used as currency.

shuowen:1765.text: To pull. Formed from reversed 廾. All characters in the 𠬜 category are formed from 𠬜. (Clerical writing now changes it to 大.)

shuowen:1766.text: To restrain or impede movement; by extension an enclosure or cage. Formed from 𠬜 and 棥; 棥 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1767.text: To restrain, 樊. Formed from 𠬜, with 䜌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1768.text: Together. Formed from 廿 and 廾. All characters in the 共 category are formed from 共.

shuowen:1769.text: To supply. Formed from 共, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1770.text: To divide. Formed from 廾 and 畀; 畀 means to give. All characters in the 異 category are formed from 異.

shuowen:1771.text: Receiving an increase when things are divided is called 戴. Formed from 異, with 𢦔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1772.text: To lift together. Formed from 𦥑 and 廾. All characters in the 舁 category are formed from 舁. Read like 余.

shuowen:1773.text: To rise high. Formed from 舁, with 囟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1774.text: A party or allies. Formed from 舁 and 与.

shuowen:1775.text: To rise. Formed from 舁 and 同, expressing shared strength.

shuowen:1776.text: Hands crossed or placed facing each other, their fingers directed inward. All characters in the 𦥑 category are formed from 𦥑. [The digital source has corrupt simplified graph components 纟 and 纠, so no literal component analysis should be asserted.]

shuowen:1777.text: The middle of the body. It depicts a person holding their waist with 𦥑. Formed from 𦥑, with abbreviated 交 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1778.text: Early dawn, when dimness clears. Formed from 𦥑 and 辰; 辰 means time and also indicates the sound. 𠃨 with 夕 makes 𡖊; 臼 with 辰 makes 䢅, both sharing the same idea. All characters in the 䢅 category are formed from 䢅.

shuowen:1779.text: To plow. Formed from 䢅, with 囟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1780.text: In Qi, cooking is called 炊爨. 𦥑 depicts holding a steamer; 冂 is the stove opening; 廾 pushes wood into the fire. All characters in the 爨 category are formed from 爨.

shuowen:1781.text: That which supports a cooking vessel. Formed from abbreviated 爨 and abbreviated 鬲.

shuowen:1782.text: A blood sacrifice. It depicts sacrifice at a stove. Formed from abbreviated 爨 and 酉; 酉 is what is used in sacrifice. Also formed from 分, which indicates the sound.

shuowen:1783.text: An animal skin treated to remove its hair, changing and renewing it. It depicts the ancient form of 革. All characters in the 革 category are formed from 革.

shuowen:1784.text: Skin with its hair removed. The Analects says: “The stripped hides of tigers and leopards.” Formed from 革, with 郭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1785.text: 靬 is dried leather. Wuwei has Lijian county. Formed from 革, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1786.text: Raw hide that can be made into binding thongs. Formed from 革, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1787.text: An artisan who softens leather. Formed from 革, with 包 indicating the sound. Read like 朴. The Rites of Zhou says: “The leather-softening craftsmen are the Bao clan.” 鞄 is the same as 鮑.

shuowen:1788.text: An artisan who works hides to make drums. Formed from 革, with 軍 indicating the sound. Read like 運.

shuowen:1789.text: Soft. Formed from 革 and 柔; 柔 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1790.text: Soft leather. Formed from 革, with 旦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1791.text: Embroidered leather. Formed from 革, with 貴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1792.text: A broad belt. The Changes says: “Perhaps he is awarded a broad belt.” Men wear leather belts; women wear silk. Formed from 革, with 般 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1793.text: To bind with leather. The Changes says: “Bind it with the hide of a yellow ox.” Formed from 革, with 巩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1794.text: The hollow leather upper or side of a shoe; by extension, a covering of leather. Formed from 革, with 免 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1795.text: A small child's shoe. Formed from 革, with 及 indicating the sound. Read like 沓.

shuowen:1796.text: 䩕角, a kind of leather shoe. Formed from 革, with 卬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1797.text: A leather shoe. Formed from 革, with 是 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1798.text: The shoe called 鞮䩡沙. Formed from 革 and 夾; 夾 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1799.text: A kind of leather shoe. Formed from 革, with 徙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1800.text: A shoe of raw leather. Formed from 革, with 奚 indicating the sound.
